identity.title: Navigating Semantic Drift in Task-Agnostic Class-Incremental Learning

problem.claim: Task-agnostic class-incremental learning must acquire new classes while retaining prior knowledge when task identity is unknown, balancing flexibility and stability.

contributions.claim: The study attributes the feature-distribution gap between novel and existing tasks primarily to differences in mean and covariance moments.
It proposes semantic drift calibration combining mean-shift compensation, covariance calibration via a Mahalanobis constraint, and feature-level self-distillation.
For mean calibration, class means are computed from sample embeddings and task shifts are estimated from proximity-weighted embedding changes relative to the previous mean.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their semantic drift calibration method as novel, distinguishing it through joint mean-shift compensation and covariance calibration.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that comprehensive experiments on commonly used datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach.

narrative_sequence.summary: CIL requires sequential acquisition of new classes while preserving previously learned knowledge.
The central difficulty is balancing flexibility and stability without a known task ID.
The authors report that novel-versus-existing task feature-distribution differences are mainly associated with mean and covariance moments.
The proposed calibration compensates mean shifts, aligns class-specific covariances, and adds feature-level self-distillation.
The authors report dataset experiments and provide source code.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a distributional gap to mean and covariance moments, then maps each component to a corresponding calibration operation.

lessons.interpretation: A compact diagnosis-to-intervention mapping can make a method’s design rationale more traceable.
lessons.application: When proposing a drift-handling method, identify measurable distributional components first and explicitly assign each component a targeted corrective mechanism.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the relevant shift is not well represented by low-order moments or when the abstract lacks evidence supporting the diagnosis.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, metrics, numerical gains, or experimental conditions behind the reported effectiveness.
It does not quantify how much of the distribution gap is explained by mean versus covariance differences.
The abstract does not provide details on the task-agnostic inference or task-shift estimation protocol beyond the stated embedding-based procedure.
